rationale: The Court is likely to hold that § 544(b)(1) is strictly derivative and requires a real unsecured creditor who could sue under applicable nonbankruptcy law, which is absent when federal sovereign immunity would bar any such suit against the United States. Section 106(a) waives immunity as a defense in properly triggered § 544 actions but does not unmistakably rewrite § 544(b)(1) to create a hypothetical creditor or expand substantive exposure.
